speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have multiple skin lesions; can you tell me how long they have been present and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; given the daycare exposure and your brother's recent chickenpox, can you describe the appearance of these lesions and whether they have any fluid-filled vesicles or scabs? REQUEST TEST: Skin_lesion_description.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Multiple skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities; lesions are firm without warmth or erythema, and there are no fluid-filled vesicles or scabs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for this viral infection, and your history of daycare exposure and a sibling with chickenpox supports a diagnosis of a common childhood viral exanthem, not appendicitis. I am requesting images of the lesions to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES.
